item.title: Requirements for complaint for probable-cause determinations
item.description:
STATE OF MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT AMENDMENT TO MAINE RULES OF UNIFIED CRIMINAL PROCEDURE
2026 Me. Rules 03
Effective: October 1, 2026
All of the Justices concurring therein, the following amendment to the Maine Rules of Unified Criminal Procedure is adopted to be effective on the date indicated above. The specific amendment is stated below. To aid in the understanding of the amendment, an Advisory Note appears after the text of the amendment. The Advisory Note states the reason for recommending the amendment, but the Advisory Note is not part of the amendment adopted by the Court.
1. Rule 4A of the Maine Rules of Unified Criminal Procedure is amended to read as follows:
RULE 4A. PROBABLE CAUSE DETERMINATION UPON WARRANTLESS ARREST FOR ANY CRIME
(a) Timing: Required Findings. Except in a bona fide emergency or other extraordinary circumstance, when a defendant arrested without a warrant for any crime is not released from custody within 48 hours after arrest, including Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, the court or justi ce of the peace shall determine, within that time period, whether there is probable cause to believe that a crime has been committed and that the arrested defendant has committed it. If the evidence does not establish such probable cause, the court or jus tice of the peace shall discharge the arrested defendant. If a probable cause determination has not taken place within 36 hours after the arrest, including Saturdays, Sundays, and legal holidays, the custodian shall notify the attorney for the State of the upcoming deadline. For purposes of this Rule “custody” means incarceration. Rule 45(a) and (b) have no application to this subdivision. (b) Evidence. item.title: Digital Archive Services
item.description: Open Access - the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives Welcome to the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives. These records include bills introduced in the Legislature, reports from the Governor's Executive Council, election returns, deeds and maps from the Maine Land Office, vital statistics prior to 1892, federal census records up to 1880, county court records dating back to 1636, and military records through World War I, among others. As of March 1, 2026, our online collection includes over one million individual records. The Maine State Archives will continue to expand this database as we digitize more of our collection. All documents are public records and are free to download.
item.content:encoded:
Open Access - the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives

Welcome to the online digital collection of the Maine State Archives. These records include bills introduced in the Legislature, reports from the Governor's Executive Council, election returns, deeds and maps from the Maine Land Office, vital statistics prior to 1892, federal census records up to 1880, county court records dating back to 1636, and military records through World War I, among others. As of March 1, 2026, our online collection includes over one million individual records. The Maine State Archives will continue to expand this database as we digitize more of our collection. All documents are public records and are free to download.

item.title: BNC Notice & Service Disruption
item.description: Thursday, October 15, 2026 The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has been experiencing a nationwide service disruption since on or about October 9, 2026, affecting all U.S. Bankruptcy Courts. The outage has interrupted the BNC's processing and delivery of notices and orders issued by the Court. As a result, parties who ordinarily receive notices and orders through the BNC may experience delays in receiving those documents. The outage is also affecting CM/ECF users' ability to generate and print a List of Creditors. The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF. At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services. Additionally, the following websites are unavailable: bnc.uscourts.gov bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov notices.uscourts.gov National Creditor Registration Service website that supports CM/ECF access to address labels The Court will provide additional updates as information becomes available.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, October 15, 2026

The Bankruptcy Noticing Center (BNC) has been experiencing a nationwide service disruption since on or about October 9, 2026, affecting all U.S. Bankruptcy Courts. The outage has interrupted the BNC's processing and delivery of notices and orders issued by the Court. As a result, parties who ordinarily receive notices and orders through the BNC may experience delays in receiving those documents. The outage is also affecting CM/ECF users' ability to generate and print a List of Creditors.

The outage does not affect the electronic delivery of Notices of Electronic Filing (NEFs), which continue to be generated and distributed normally through CM/ECF.

At this time, there is no estimated date or time for restoration of services. 

Additionally, the following websites are unavailable:

  • bnc.uscourts.gov
  • bankruptcynotices.uscourts.gov
  • notices.uscourts.gov
  • National Creditor Registration Service website that supports CM/ECF access to address labels

The Court will provide additional updates as information becomes available.
